newsitem.title: GREECE: SOCCER-OLYMPIAKOS "WINTER CHAMPIONS" WITH DISPUTED PENALTY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OLYMPIAKOS "WINTER CHAMPIONS" WITH DISPUTED PENALTY.

text.p: Olympiakos Piraeus, Greece's most popular soccer club, were declared "winter champions" on Monday after beating Kavala with a disputed penalty.
"Winter champions with a false penalty," said the Athens Sportime newspaper of the Sunday first division match that left Olympiakos leading the standings at mid-season.
"Kavala, the better of the two sides lost to Olympiakos with a penalty invented by the referee," the paper said.
The referee ordered the penalty in the 80th minute when Olympiakos striker Alekos Alexandris fell inside the box. Grigoris Georgatos converted the spot kick and Olympiakos won 2-1.
Television showed Alexandris was not tackled by any Kavala defender.
Olympiakos, who last won the Greek championship in 1987, this season signed the most respected coach in Greece, Serb Dusan Bayevic, and many leading players.
"I want to see the disputed moment again on video and if it was no penalty I'll come out and say it," Bayevic said.
Kavala players were seen crying in the dressing rooms after the match.
"I feel ashamed of the way big teams beat smaller ones in Greek soccer," Kavala coach George Parashos said. "Olympiakos is a big club and should not need help by the referee to win."
Olympiakos share first place in the standings on 39 points with bitter rivals Panathinaikos but have the advantage as they beat Panathinaikos 1-0 last month.
